genesis.11.p1.b1.text: Now the whole world had one language and a common form of speech. And as people journeyed eastward, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.

genesis.11.p1.b2.text: And they said to one another, “Come, let us make bricks and bake them thoroughly.”

genesis.11.p1.b3.text: So they used brick instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar.

genesis.11.p2.b4.text: “Come,” they said, “let us build for ourselves a city with a tower that reaches to the heavens, that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.”

genesis.11.p3.b5.text: Then the LORD came down to see the city and the tower that the sons of men were building.

genesis.11.p3.b6.text: If they have begun to do this as one people speaking the same language, then nothing they devise will be beyond them.

genesis.11.p3.b7.text: Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.”

genesis.11.p4.b9.text: That is why it is called Babel, for there the LORD confused the language of the whole world, and from that place the LORD scattered them over the face of all the earth.

genesis.11.p5.b10.text: This is the account of Shem. Two years after the flood, when Shem was 100 years old, he became the father of Arphaxad.

genesis.11.p5.b11.text: When Nahor was 29 years old, he became the father of Terah.

genesis.11.p5.b12.text: When Terah was 70 years old, he became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.

genesis.11.p6.b13.text: And Haran became the father of Lot. During his father Terah’s lifetime, Haran died in his native land, in Ur of the Chaldeans.

genesis.11.p6.b14.text: But Sarai was barren; she had no children.

genesis.11.p6.b15.text: And Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot son of Haran, and his daughter-in-law Sarai the wife of Abram, and they set out from Ur of the Chaldeans for the land of Canaan …

genesis.11.p6.b16.text: But when they arrived in Haran, they settled there. Terah lived 205 years, and he died in Haran.
